rationale: This collapses the archive's cash-value interactions into a single dimensionally incoherent ratio (subtracting a flow, depreciation, from stocks of cash and current liabilities) and is otherwise a rediscovery of the well-known net-cash/net-current-asset-to-price value measure with no genuine cross-theme structure.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, and the static retained-earnings-to-liabilities overlay is economically distinct from the archive's flow-based dividend coverage signal, though it remains an incremental variation on the same dividend-yield-times-solvency template and is close to the known retained-earnings/distress-conditioned value literature.

The anchor switch from sales yield to earnings yield is a substantive, well-diagnosed response to the archive's sign conflict (cheap revenue loading on distressed low-margin firms) and the expression matches the hypothesis, though margin-stability-conditioned earnings yield sits near the established quality-value/earnings-stability literature and the 3-period VOL term will further thin already low coverage.

This is the archive's best-performing Maintenance-Light Cash Value with only the value anchor swapped and an identical overlay, so it reads as a cosmetic variant rather than a diagnosed improvement, and the overlay is partly mechanical since depreciation is added back inside oancf.

Conditioning high book-to-market on an improving retained-earnings-to-liabilities trend is effectively Piotroski's value-plus-financial-strength strategy (rising profitability plus falling leverage) rediscovered, and retained earnings is itself a component of the ceq numerator, creating mechanical overlap with the value anchor.

Expression, hypothesis, and expected sign are mutually consistent with adequate coverage, and net working capital scaled by total liabilities is a genuinely different liquidity overlay from the archive's cash-flow-coverage and current-liability-change variants, though it is close to the Altman-style distress screen and to the broader distress-conditioned value idea.
